To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the current P2P traffic has very different characteristics from traditional client-server traffic, (2) the traffic is highly bursty and shows significant locality, (3) the traffic is asymmetric and shows significant locality in the reverse direction, (4) the P2P applications show significant locality in content requests, and (5) the locality of content requests is different from the locality of the traffic.
the P2P system we studied is scalable and efficient.

P2P systems are a new class of network application that is fundamentally different from traditional client-server systems, and that the performance of P2P systems depends on a number of factors including the number of users, the number of peers per user, the amount of data stored per peer, and the amount of data downloaded per user.
